item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Mirror Cyborgs
item.content:encoded:
Good notes, I'll go back to what worked and come up with alternatives for what did not work.

But about Anderson, yes it's been stated how he uses magic, but where did that magic come from? If Methane is the god of machines, I mean not just a giant robot that claims to be a god but actually a divine entity that can actually be defined as a god, then wouldn't it be possible that Anderson's technology could fall under his domain? I was actually coming at this from a "God works in mysterious ways" approach, maybe Anderson didn't realize he was taking the power of a god when he first found his magic, but what he did still got the God's attention.

As for the plot holes around 3560, I thought about that. I believe it hasn't actually been found yet so it's claims would refer to a place that the Foundation isn't aware of yet, so it would refer to it's world in a more oblique way that makes sense to the reader but not to the in universe characters, at least not yet. Also, yes the inhabitants turn intangible when removed, but there is evidence that there are exceptions when they go hunting individuals for a reason. 2806 isn't made with the awareness that they are pulling from that dimension(Vincent and Phone as were working off studying magic without realizing the methods would summon spirits from another dimension to animate their creations or that the other dimension would come back for them), although Vincent himself suggests that tracking similar energy would help the Foundation track the instances still unaccounted for which means he may at least suspect a connection even if he's not aware. So the idea was that 2806 is animated by 3560, which is why they appear in disrepair, the parts of their souls are being borrowed to animate partial robotics. Imagine that saying "Integrate" to activate the Gyrfalcon actually summons a robot spirit to inhabit the physical construct. It would be like Taily-po, and the rest of the robot spirit is trying to get his Taily-po and is able to come get him the same way the other spirits would later come to take the Anderson traitors and thus be an exception that remains tangible because it has a specific tie to something in this world.

I thought I had this thought out, I've been researching this for two months and I thought I had this worked out. If I missed something important please provide a link. If I can't work around this, I will remove Anderson altogether and start this over as completely original, but I wanted to tie together existing lore. Every time I read a cyborg article with unclear origins I wonder who made this thing because it had to be made by someone and then Anderson and CotBG seem to cover it well and any SCP that strays makes me wonder what poor soul is making these machines and will they ever find their home in the universe with the other anomalous machines?

item.title: Re: [Seeking Greenlights]Intergalactic Flushing Service
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Central Narrative: I haven't really thought of this, and to be honest I don't think I really need one.

You do need one yeah; you're trying to write a short story about a weird thing, not an encylcopedia entry on it; and so what you do with the anomaly is more important than what the anomaly does.

I want to include a long list of experimentations referencing other space-related SCPs, and possibly hint at some side effects / alternate anomalous properties this object might have along the way.

So like, what are the side effects? What are the alternate anomalous properties? What other space-related SCPs? What's tying your experiments together so it feels like a cohesive whole and not just a random series of experiments?

My central concern is that as far as anomalous stuff goes, this almost feels more like an anomalous item: it has a very simple thing what it does and there's not a lot of like, things you can do to explore it. The hinting towards experiment logs could be enough to fix this but honestly I don't really have enough of a feel for what you're doing with them or how you're wanting them to be funny to tell if it'd work.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello SpookyBonez! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It seems that YouTube is quite the introduction power to this site; you'd be surprised how many people discover SCP through videos, and it's really awesome to see that we achieved such a wide audience. If you're going to push further in writing for the site, you'll want to click that little red collapsible at the bottom of this comment - there, you'll find a plethora of useful resources created for the purpose of guiding new members of the site towards guides and other resources which will definitely help you improve your writing and seek help on it.

Without further ado though, let's actually click it, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: Anomalous Chime Seeking Greenlight.
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Post-haste our illustrious Foundation secures the area and is now able to devote its energy to a favored past-time: testing logs. Including but not limited to logs from the personnel/civilians on the ground, and logs from the Foundation's bunker where testing can be conducted on D-Class in peace.

I guess my big concern is: what are these testing logs showing? It kinda feels like they might feel…pedestrian; but I think a few showcasing the various melodies it produces could be a fun little middle section.

We also have a neat little epilogue with the arrest of the two individuals responsible, and the return of the children to the foster care system.

Uhhh what children? Are they just a some children who are enamoured by the clock or?

become obsessive with the clock, and may begin to prioritize listening to the chime over basic bodily needs.

this feels to me like it's…perhaps a very dark turn for a supposedly light hearted scp to take

I don't necessarily hate the idea of this; and a lot of this feels like it comes close to working; but it feels like it's missing something to just really kick it over the line and I'm not quite sure what?

The test logs feeling awkwardly inserted between the discovery section and the epilogue might be the core issue; but it might be that there's not a huge feeling of purpose to this: it might just need some kinda hint as to why the two people responsible made this and what they were intending, y'know?

item.title: An in-depth report into the structure of the Foundation.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre: Factual, Informative

Page Layout: Report title and brief summary of purpose, note from report's author, tier explanation, 05 council, ethics committee, administrator, general high level staff

Elevator Pitch: A report commissioned by the 05 council simplifying and explaining how the different branches of the SCP Foundation interact and their relevant powers and duties. The report will contain an explanation of the 05 council, the ethics committee, the administrator and all their associated staff as well as my own idea for classifying the different levels of authority in the Foundation (this system is currently only planned to be used within the context of the report).

Central Narrative: A factual report written by a high level member of staff under the orders of the 05 council.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Provides an understanding of several mysterious and poorly understood groups and individuals.

Additional Notes: This information varies between cannons so I will only be able to apply my own personal interpretation. I already have notes on paper but I do not want to commit to a draft until I hear some early feedback from the community.

item.title: Re: Carnivorous Tattoo
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

I kinda like the core of this idea; the way the tattoo works and what it does, and the angle of it being a victim of a biker gang getting revenge and stuff works for me.

The narrative does not: it's perhaps a personal thing but I generally do not like when all of the central narrative in an article is backstory: my general preference is that the Foundation are the protagonists of the story since the article is written from their POV; and so everything has to be centred around what they know.

My other concern with it is that it feels very flat: there's no emotional highs or escalation or anything; so it just kinda feels like a sequence of events that happen without it feeling like it's building up to something or going somewhere; and so the ending feels very conclusive but almost unearned because there's not really any kinda sense of catharsis or w/e when it's finally contained.

So yeah: my advice is that this has elements which work, and it feels like a good setting for a story; but it also feels like the actual narrative isn't quite there: it feels like there's this opportunity for a great SCP-4205 style story; where we see the Foundation struggling to contain this or w/e or someone affected by it slowly like, coming to terms with their imminent death; and it kinda feels like you have the angle for this but not necessarily the meat of the agents emotional arc?

I'm having in-universe theories be proposed as to the nature of the anomaly right off the bat for the reader to contemplate as things move forward.
A few to chew on, if you're curious:
Men in the Mirror - GoI-PCS has avoided detection due to being a recently-formed anomalous group based on the SCP Foundation.

Natural Course - GoI-PCS has avoided detection by adapting the same protocols over time, making them equally as proficient in remaining undetected.

Corporate Espionage - GoI-PCS has avoided detection by gathering information on our protocols and applying these to themselves.

Thaumiel-Esque - GoI-PCS has avoided detection through the use of an anomaly or anomalies that conceal them in some manner, and similarities are coincidental.

And the couple that come up later:

I Am My Greatest Enemy: GoI-PCS is a facility that belonged to the SCP Foundation and was left to rot, then rebuilt itself into its own organization.

Me, Myself, and You: GoI-PCS is a SCP Foundation facility that IS an anomaly, but that anomaly is that it is repeatedly forgotten, then rediscovered. This occurs due to the both of them repeatedly amnesticizing each other.

hope that helps (=

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight for my idea: The fibonacci watch
item.content:encoded:
The first narrative section feels a lot stronger to me than the second section, in that, it actually has a character and them growing and changing and being affected by this in an emotional way; whereas the second narrative section is really just a bunch of boring tests that convey that hey, this anomaly works exactly as y'know, we were told it works; with a cross-link to a work that's…not really adding much to either piece.

The problem with the first narrative section is that you can't actually show a lot of the interesting bits in a SCP article: the Foundation isn't really involved in the story, so you kinda have to rely on the person wearing the watch telling us about it, y'know? So my advice here is really 'figure out how you can use the narrative framework of the second section to convey the emotional impact of the first.

I'd also recommend getting rid of the crosstesting: it's generally a bad idea to mix two anomalies when you aren't sure how it'll play out; and so it's generally frowned upon to do it. Beyond this, the actual crosstesting doesn't add much: it's just another random example of this doing the expected thing that's not really that interesting alone.

So like, what does the Foundation do here? I'm really trying to get a feel for whether you've thought about the specifics of the narrative and like, how this is going to play out.

juxtaposed with what the initial squadrons were perceiving as life

My concern here is like…how does the Foundation know this? How are you conveying this? Is it just a kinda retrospective of this via interviews after the fact or?

At it's core, I like a lot of what this is trying to do as a whole; but it feels…perhaps like it needs a narrower focus? Like, there's kinda a mix of 'this affects a big area and a tonne of people' and the narrower, almost personal, focus of 'the effect of losing the best year of your life' and like, either of these could work but it feels like blending the two might be a little awkward?

Something about this lasting exactly one year feels…odd to me. Like if it had been a short time, a few days or a few hours say, I'd be very 'well it's a temporary thing it makes sense'; whereas if it had been forever say, it'd feel like a permanent thing; and a year is weirdly trapped between the two so it feels very long for a temporary effect?

item.title: Re: GOC Threat Entity Entry (India/China)
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

But I can't really dedicate myself to figuring out how to write this draft into this format without the green lights for the concept first. That's what the Drafts and Critiques forum is for, right?

Uhhh sort of but not really; the drafts critique forum is for giving feedback on this as a draft and assumes you have attempted to answer the question of 'how do you get this into the format' already. Whereas I want to know you've at least considered it because guess what buddy: the format imposes restrictions on how you can tell the story; and if you don't consider how those restrictions are gonna impact the story telling, you're gonna have a bad day when you try to write this.

As for the actual longer form exploration, I'm kinda…torn on it. If executed well, this could be really good, and I can totally see this working well; but it feels like is has a lot of potential to be really dry and boring, and I think what'll really elevate this is the characterisation: making everyone really feel real, and showing enough of the monster that it feels like a viable threat; and like…really having us understand why what's happening is interesting.

I'm still really not convinced by this as a goi-format: it really feels like a lot of this detail would be best kept as a tale; since like, it feels like a lot of times this would be quiet informal stuff you don't necessarily want to admit to doing in an official report (e.g., the two indian soldiers being ordered to shoot the chinese ones if they return alone).

I will greenlight this under the assumption you deeply think about how you tell this story and really consider what the best format for it is.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight for Attention Seeking Dog
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

I kinda like the anomaly here, at least, part of it: the idea of this being a thing that people perceive as just being a like, regular lovely dog and not a dessicated corpse is kinda fun; the rest feels ehh. Like, I don't think making it a permanent effect, or the corpse screaming when it's harmed, or even the idea of it like effectively forcing people to play with it, particularly add a tonne here in a way that's good.

This brings me to the central narrative section: this feels like it's exploring this in the least interesting way; I'm in general not really a fan of articles which open as if they're about one set of anomalous properties but quickly change to being about something completely different. But it feels to me that having this like,,, almost slightly surreal horror where people are acting like this SCP is completely normal and very cool whilst it's literally falling apart in front of them would be a lot more effective: see e.g. SCP-2790 for the kinda style you could pull off to achieve this.

If you wanted to keep everything which you have currently, you'll need to find a way to make this feel like it ends in a way that grants more closure: the kinda, passive nature of the second mental breakdown feels very open ended and like, not necessarily a bad thing to have happen, but it feels like it's still kinda the middle of the story and that the elements need to end up going somewhere satisfying, y'know.

item.title: Re: An in-universe parody of Are We Cool Yet.
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

matching the actual effects of the statue becoming more nonsensical and racking up a larger body count in the process. Eventually the statue starts just killing people at random for seemingly no reason

I'm a little hesitant about this aspect because like….it feels like the Foundation should be better equipped to handle this?

the foundation eventually works out that they have inadvertently been led on a wild goose chase, and deduce the item was meant as a parody of AWCY themselves

this feels…perhaps odd to me; like…I kinda get how this works as a parody of AWCY? but it feels like, the whole angle of it leading the foundation on a wild goose chase feels like the actual parody angle of the object is too subtle in universe: like, generally if you're doing a parody, you want people to know it's a parody and enjoy it as such; rather than to trick them into reacting like it's real right up until you pull the curtain back and go 'sike', y'know?

Part of me also feels like the Foundation is a lot more likely to ask 'how do we get this to stop' than 'what is the artist trying to say' and I'm a little unsure of the focus here as a result.

I think there's a small part of me that feels like doing a genuinely confusing artistic piece sincerely; like, the kind of anart piece that genuinely defies meaning and which the foundation attempts to understand the why of might be more interesting than treating it as a parody of AWCY?; and like, having this as an exploration of what art is would be more interesting but *shrugs*.

Alternatively: the idea of this being a thing to make fun of AWCY? feels actually fun and I think taking this in a lot more comedic route could help; where like, instead of being just 'a bunch of actual AWCY? things slapped together weirdly', it's like, a deliberately incompetently done piece? Where you actually like, play up the comedy a lot more and deliberately make this a funny article about a weird thing: like almost using the classic comedy duo thing of the SCP being the comedy provider and the Foundation being the straight man, y'know?

item.title: Re: The Automill (seeking greenligh)
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

The bread is anomalous, and when consumed, results in effects ranging from mildly annoying, such as sneezing every minute for day, to catasthrophic, such turing the subjects lungs into baguettes.

My concern with this is that, broad effects like this where the scp can do basically anything are really hard to pull off well: if you establish that like, anything can happen when the bread is consumed, then you make it really hard to make anything that does happen be interesting. It also makes it hard to have a good sense of escalation to the items produced because like…there's no feeling of this getting worse over time or anything.

Central Narrative

See, what I'm really looking for in the 'Central Narrative' section is an answer to the question: 'what is in the article beyond just describing the SCP?'; and so the narrative section just being you expanding more on what the SCP does is a red flag to me because it implies you aren't intending doing anything interesting with the SCP.

My hot advice here is that you're trying to write an interesting short story about a weird thing, not a DnD style monster manual entry for it; and so what you do with the SCP is far, far more important than what the SCP does.

Which ties into my first concern: the breadth of what this SCP does is so wide that trying to figure out what's interesting about it might be really hard; and I would suggest may considering narrowing it a lot. Like, it feels like the interesting thing might be to explore why this SCP produces bread, and it can just…anomalously manufacture bread without the bread itself being anomalous to do allow that? It might also be worth considering whether there'd be like…anything interesting about how the bread is made: like, maybe the materials come from somewhere and you can use that as like, an interesting angle to explore?

item.title: Re: Data not redacted? (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
This feels very reminiscent of stuff like SCP-5242 or Allison Eckhart and I'm sure there's something that plays with the core a lot more closely than either of those; and so I'm left feeling very much like this needs to do a touch more with the idea.

The angle of this being like, the Ethics Committee trying to get the upper hand over the O5's is a pretty good angle and I think it could really help this work but I don't really have a feel for how this article is going to convey that: it's kinda thrown in as a possibility in the hook section; but like, are you going to be somewhat explicit about this? Are you just going to hint towards it? Is it just a possible hypothesis you think a reader might come up with?

I guess at the end of the day, my core question is really: so what are you doing with this? There's like a lot of like, vague hypothesises mentioned in this and they all sound vaguely interesting but I don't really have an idea of how this is all going to come together to form a cohesive article that actually like, tells a story, y'know?
